stale_or_missing_flag.v: flag fresh (age <= 0.3 s, ASSUMED: 3 frames at the 10 Hz minimum): PRIMED -> plan 0.81 s, UNPRIMED -> plan 1.41 s. Flag stale or missing at T_fire: hold the last valid flag received since the MECO valve closure (UNPRIMED -> 1.41 s, PRIMED -> 0.81 s); no valid flag since MECO -> 0.81 s. The plan is evaluated every frame (trigger when the predicted time to go <= plan + rise) and latched at T_fire; a flip to UNPRIMED after the 1.41 s trigger point fires at once.
stale_or_missing_flag.note: GNC decision, the safer plan for a stale or missing flag: hold the last valid flag, default 0.81 s. A stale flag is one fault (the ECU->FC link or the ECU publisher); holding PRIMED is wrong only if a second, independent fault (an emptying of the primed segment that the ECU did not report before the flag went stale) coincides with it, which costs the fault-path loss. A held UNPRIMED errs only in the safe direction: the segment re-primes only through the NC valve (opening, or an inflow seat leak), and an unreported re-prime costs the false-UNPRIMED loss (P stays >= the false_unprimed rows), not the fault-path loss. Planning 1.41 s on every stale flag (maximin) costs that loss on every primed flight with a stale flag to cover a double fault; it is the better expected choice only when the probability of an unreported emptying exceeds q* (q_star_range).

drogue_line: the line attaches only at the nose tip on the vehicle axis (swivel + release); no bridle leg, line or release lanyard runs along the body toward the engine bay

stale_or_missing_flag.rule: flag fresh (age <= 0.3 s, ASSUMED: 3 frames at the 10 Hz minimum): PRIMED -> plan 0.81 s, UNPRIMED -> plan 1.41 s. Flag stale or missing at T_fire: hold the last valid flag received since the MECO valve closure (UNPRIMED -> 1.41 s, PRIMED -> 0.81 s); no valid flag since MECO -> 0.81 s. The plan is evaluated every frame (trigger when the predicted time to go <= plan + rise) and latched at T_fire; a flip to UNPRIMED after the 1.41 s trigger point fires at once.
stale_or_missing_flag.decision: GNC decision, the safer plan for a stale or missing flag: hold the last valid flag, default 0.81 s. A stale flag is one fault (the ECU->FC link or the ECU publisher); holding PRIMED is wrong only if a second, independent fault (an emptying of the primed segment that the ECU did not report before the flag went stale) coincides with it, which costs the fault-path loss. A held UNPRIMED errs only in the safe direction: the segment re-primes only through the NC valve (opening, or an inflow seat leak), and an unreported re-prime costs the false-UNPRIMED loss (P stays >= the false_unprimed rows), not the fault-path loss. Planning 1.41 s on every stale flag (maximin) costs that loss on every primed flight with a stale flag to cover a double fault; it is the better expected choice only when the probability of an unreported emptying exceeds q* (q_star_range).
conditions: the ECU publishes a distinct UNKNOWN (P_feed invalid) state, or publishes UNPRIMED whenever it will run the prep at RELIGHT; the FC treats UNKNOWN as UNPRIMED
the flag is valid only after the MECO valve closure (no flag value from the ascent burn)
the staleness limit and the flag rate are Electronics' to confirm (ASSUMED 0.3 s, >= 10 Hz)

the seat-leak drain time of the segment is unknown: if Electronics shows that an emptying can start and finish inside the staleness limit, the double-fault argument weakens and the maximin plan should be reconsidered
